clue.text: The Full Monty

parts.note: read as a name: Monty is the short form, so the full version of that name is wanted, as for the wartime field marshal nicknamed Monty

explanation.surface: The title of the film about unemployed Sheffield steelworkers who strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is the bait; read 'Full' literally and the clue asks for the longer name of which Monty is the familiar short form, famously Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty is the usual nickname for the surname, so its complete, unshortened form is the full Monty.

clue.text: Money for major road development's far from settled

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major north-south motorway, written MI
a grant is money given for a project

explanation.surface: Funding for building a motorway is still a long way from being agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway from London to Yorkshire, with the 1 read as the letter I; a grant is money for its development.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant moves from place to place, so is the opposite of someone settled.

clue.text: Song, leading single?

parts.note: a number is a song in a show or concert
one is single, a lone unit

explanation.surface: A song described as the top-selling record in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Song and single suggest the pop charts, where a chart-topping record is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one describes whatever comes first or foremost, the top of a ranking.

clue.text: From here, many fly flag, finally, at place up North to show Navy's left

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of flag

parts.note: taken as written
Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland
to air an opinion is to show it publicly
port is the naval word for the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A northern town displays the flag to show where the Navy has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Wick is a town in Caithness, northern Scotland. The answer is London's second airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Large numbers of passengers take flights out of this airport south of London.

clue.text: Spymaster's thrown, given inappropriate role

parts.note: M is the spymaster heading the secret service in the Bond stories, and the 's stands for is
to cast is to throw

explanation.surface: A spy chief has been thrown off balance by being given an unsuitable job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spymaster's' reads as M IS: M is James Bond's chief, and the apostrophe-s is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor miscast has been put in a part that does not suit them.

clue.text: Uninhabited island comes as shock to everyone

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock them
all means everyone

explanation.surface: News of a deserted isle stuns the whole population.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall is a tiny rocky islet in the North Atlantic, west of Scotland, with no residents.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a bare granite islet in the Atlantic where nobody lives.

clue.text: Bloomers made here in Coventry

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the letters of the following place name

explanation.surface: A remark that ladies' underwear is manufactured in a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are long loaves of bread here, not knickers; the letters sit inside 'Coventry', the West Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a crusty loaf, and bread is baked in this kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Very old vehicle — terms reduced by 50%

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi

explanation.surface: An ancient car and a cut in the price terms by half.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself shortened: the answer is the clipped form of a word for one's stock of terms, about half its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocab is a colloquial shortening of vocabulary, the stock of words someone knows, roughly halving the word.

clue.text: Additional crowd creating a stir in the capital once

definitions.text: a stir in the capital once

parts.note: new can mean additional, as in a new supply
the gate is the crowd attending a sporting event

explanation.surface: An extra throng caused excitement in London long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for prison, not commotion; Newgate was London's notorious prison until 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, and this was a famous London jail, now demolished.

clue.text: King may be drunk, having equivalent of twenty bottles of wine

definitions.meaning: a king of Babylon in the Old Testament

definitions.text: may be drunk, having equivalent of twenty bottles of wine
definitions.meaning: a very large wine bottle holding the contents of twenty standard bottles, whose contents may be drunk

explanation.surface: A monarch might be intoxicated after consuming a vast quantity of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a drunken king; really it is two meanings, the Babylonian king and the giant bottle named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Babylonian ruler lends his name to the largest standard champagne bottle, holding fifteen litres.

clue.text: Full scale rejection of union by publication

indicators.note: a rejection throws something back, so the union beside the publication is read backwards as one run

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A union's comprehensive turning-down of a newspaper's proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns TU (union) with MAG (publication) beside it, TUMAG, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the whole range of something, originally the complete musical scale.

clue.text: Scared, slightly affected by bully — one given undue respect

indicators.note: the word Scared is only a little altered, its letters gently rearranged

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them

explanation.surface: Someone a little frightened after being pushed around, an object of excessive deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly affected' is apt: only two letters of the first word change places. 'bully' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution held above criticism, revered beyond what it deserves.

clue.text: New World collection in a camera shot

indicators.note: shot here means ruined or wrecked, so the letters of in a camera are scrambled

explanation.surface: A collection from the Americas captured in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like photography, fitting 'camera', but signals the rearrangement of IN A CAMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and objects connected with America, the New World, gathered as a collection.

clue.text: Shadow cast by partner finally being replaced in dance

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so a letter of the dance is shifted within it

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of partner

explanation.surface: A dark figure appears when one's dancing partner is finally substituted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partner finally' is R; 'being replaced in' moves the R of RUMBA from the front to the fourth place.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, especially in an eclipse.

clue.text: Files kept in this? Assumed to hold 50

indicators.note: to hold means one piece contains another, so the Roman fifty goes inside

parts.note: I took it that... means I assumed, so took it can mean assumed
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone presumes that a folder contains fifty documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Files here are metal tools for smoothing, not documents; 'to hold' puts L (50) inside TOOK IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a hand tool, and tools are stored in this box or bag, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Port very accepted by the French race

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to hare is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: A port is welcomed by the French at a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' could be the drink, which 'accepted' supports; it is the harbour. 'accepted by' puts the V inside the article and the racing animal's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in Normandy, at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: One playing kit

parts.note: a kit is a small pocket fiddle once used by dancing masters, so someone playing it plays a bowed string instrument

explanation.surface: Someone using a set of drums or sports equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit suggests a drum kit or sports gear; it is an old miniature fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit is a tiny fiddle, so its player is a performer on a fiddle.

clue.text: Transformed himself in this art school

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of himself are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man changed his own identity while studying at an art college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges HIMSELF; 'in this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The painters of Flanders, such as Van Eyck and Rubens, form a recognised tradition of art.

clue.text: Man getting upset by woman in a state

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down entry the man's name is read upwards

parts.note: Rolf is a man's name
Ida is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man becomes distressed about a woman while in an agitated condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' sounds like being agitated, but a state is a US state. 'getting upset' turns ROLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is a state in the south-east of the USA.

clue.text: Raised money abroad poor journalist put on horse

indicators.note: in a down entry, put on means placed above, so the journalist comes first

parts.note: a hack is a poor-quality journalist

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down entry the currency is read upwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan, money abroad

explanation.surface: A badly paid reporter bets foreign cash he raised on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the Japanese currency upwards in this down entry, and 'put on' sets the journalist on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is a breed of light carriage horse, or a horse for ordinary riding.

clue.text: Just the place for the rest of one's retirement

definitions.text: Just the place for the rest of one's retirement

parts.words: Just the place for the rest of one's retirement
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed at night, and rest is sleep, so this is the room where one retires each night

explanation.surface: Advice on where to spend one's remaining years after stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement suggests leaving work for old age, but it is the nightly retirement to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: One retires to sleep in the room with the bed, the obvious place to rest.

clue.text: See big possibility with drug, so invest

indicators.note: a possibility is one of several ways things might be, so the letters of See big are arranged another way

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Spotting a big opportunity with a drug, so putting money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' looks financial, fitting 'possibility', but here means lay siege to. 'possibility' rearranges SEE BIG, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is the old military sense of surrounding it with troops to cut it off.

clue.text: Make slip, perhaps, fail to catch properly

definitions.meaning: to err by taking in one word as another, making a slip of the ear
not to pick up words correctly when listening

explanation.surface: Instructions to make an error or not quite grasp something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' suggests a ball; here it means hearing what someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: To get words wrong when listening is a slip of hearing, and is failing to catch what was said.

clue.text: When game is over, king's found in deck

indicators.note: found in means discovered inside, so the king's letter goes within the turned game
over means turned over, so the game is read backwards

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: After a card game ends, the king is discovered in the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns POLO to OLOP and 'found in' puts R inside it. Deck is a ship's floor, not a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Name put in hat — a girl's name

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes within the hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone's name drawn from a hat: a girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Lid is informal for a hat; 'put in' places N inside it, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a common female first name.

clue.text: War paint that is with things old Cheyenne leader returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation of scilicet, meaning that is or namely
items are things

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Cheyenne

explanation.surface: A Cheyenne chief, coming home with belongings, applied war paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War paint' suggests Cheyenne warriors, but is jokey slang for make-up. 'returned' turns SC + ITEMS + O + C, giving C O SMETI CS.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is humorous slang for make-up applied to the face.

clue.text: One caring terribly about a lack of education

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of One caring are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who cares deeply about the absence of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ONE CARING; 'about a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance means not knowing things, the state of being unschooled or uninformed.

clue.text: Last unknown river in the country

parts.note: in algebra the unknowns are x, y and z, so the last of them is z
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A final mystery river is somewhere within the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was the name of the central African nation now called the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: A return of service a long way out

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the service is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis serve is hit back far beyond the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of service' is tennis talk, but the service is the RAF, turned by 'return of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great distance.

clue.text: Kind author that produces lots of characters

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a writer is an author

explanation.surface: A generous novelist who creates many people in her books.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters are people in a novel on the surface, but letters typed on a page in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This machine strikes letters, or characters, onto paper one key at a time.
